title: 아파트 앞에서: 주말에 어디 가요?
objective: Say where you are going and why with -으러/-러 (e.g. 빵을 사러 빵집에 가요).
summary: Two neighbours meet outside their apartment and say where they are going and why.
setting: Saturday morning, in front of an apartment building. Two neighbours, 민수 and 마리아, meet on their way out.

task.title: SAY WHERE AND WHY
task.line: Use -으러 after a stem with a final consonant (except ㄹ) and -러 after a stem without one or ending in ㄹ (놀러), then add the place and 가요.

words.meaning: Where are you going? (a casual greeting when you meet someone outside)
words.exampleMeaning: Where are you going now? — I'm going home.

words.meaning: go (somewhere) to do something; -으러 after a final consonant (먹으러), -러 after a vowel or ㄹ (사러, 놀러)
words.exampleMeaning: In the evening I'm going (out) to meet a friend.
There is a bakery in front of my house.
There are a lot of people in the park on Sundays.
What are you doing this weekend?

words.meaning: Have a good (weekend, holiday, etc.) — said when parting

dialogue.meaning: Hi, Maria! Where are you going?

dialogue.korean: 안녕하세요. 빵을 사러 빵집에 가요. 민수 씨는요?
dialogue.meaning: Hi. I'm going to the bakery to buy bread. How about you, Minsu?

dialogue.korean: 저는 운동하러 공원에 가요. 마리아 씨는 주말에 보통 뭐 해요?
dialogue.meaning: I'm going to the park to work out. What do you usually do on weekends, Maria?

dialogue.korean: 보통 집에서 청소하고 빨래해요. 그런데 오늘은 빵을 사고 친구하고 점심을 먹으러 식당에 가요.
dialogue.meaning: I usually clean and do laundry at home. But today I'm buying bread and then going to a restaurant to have lunch with a friend.
Sounds nice. Well then, have a good weekend.

exercises: Fill in the blank with 읽다 + -으러/-러: 책을 ____ 도서관에 가요.
Choose the correct form: ①사진을 (찍으러 / 찍러) 공원에 가요. / ②커피를 (마시으러 / 마시러) 카페에 가요.
Answer 어디 가요? in Korean with -으러/-러, using the words given: ①우체국, 편지를 보내다 / ②학교, 한국어를 배우다
answers: ① 편지를 보내러 우체국에 가요. (우체국에 편지를 보내러 가요.) ② 한국어를 배우러 학교에 가요. (학교에 한국어를 배우러 가요.)
